description: Hi everyone! We’re a high school team based in Los Angeles. We have a wide range of interests including healthcare, technology, and engineering. We hope to use technology and art to make science more accessible in the digital age.
summary:
For our project, we developed an interactive narrative game following a boy that discovers a mysterious diary entry from his grandpa, describing his old love, “Sojourner”. We flashback 30 years to his grandpa’s work at NASA, where players engage in a series of mini-games to build the Sojourner Rover. In the end, the rover is launched and successfully lands on Mars. As we return to the present, the boy is inspired by the story for his science fair, while the grandpa reminisces about the Sojourner, hoping to see it again one day. 

Through our game, we wanted to combine scientific education and engaging storytelling. Our games introduce the engineering mechanics required to construct the rover, while our story aims to humanize the machines that have been sent to space. We hope that our project can encourage younger audiences to become interested in the science behind NASA projects, along with appreciating the past technology that has allowed modern space exploration to reach where it is today.
details:
Story Summary: 

A young boy is cleaning his attic when he finds a mysterious diary called “My Love, Sojourner”. He is confused as that isn’t his current grandma’s name, and he goes to talk to his grandpa. The grandpa begins to tell his story of when he worked at NASA on the Pathfinder Project, and we flashback to 30 years ago. 

We meet a younger version of the grandpa at the NASA headquarters. He leads the players through five mini-games, each designed to build a key part of the rover. Text-boxes with descriptions of each component appear on the screen as they are selected. Once the entire rover has been completed, the players are able to launch Sojourner and watch it land successfully on the surface of Mars. 

Returning to the present day, the boy decides to use Sojourner’s story for his science fair project. The grandpa comments on the many more machines that are still in space, wondering if he could one day see Sojourner again. 

Mini-Games: 

  1. Chassis Deck 
  2. Rocker-Bogie Suspension
  3. Motors
  4. Brain and Power Systems
  5. Cameras and Spectrometer 

Tools: 

Coding Languages: 

  • HTML
  • CSS
  • Javascript 

AI Agents: 

  • ChatGPT: Code, Images
  • Gemini: Research, Organization
  • Claude Code: Code 

Benefits and Impact: 

  • Audience: The game is targeted towards younger audiences and school-aged children, with the science and vocabulary designed to be both accurate and age-appropriate 
  • Interactive Learning: Players are able to learn the names and purpose of each component, getting the opportunity to assemble each part of the rover 
  • Community: We hope that the project will be able to inspire interest in STEM and engineering from children, along with bringing awareness to the machinery and equipment still left in space tod
